passages.text: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.
passages.sermon:
The house of God is a holy place.
Guard your steps when you go there.
Be careful as you approach God’s house.
Draw near to listen.
Do not rush to offer a sacrifice like fools do.
Fools offer sacrifices without understanding.
Fools do not know they do wrong.
passages.original: שְׁמֹ֣ר רַגְלֶיךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר תֵּלֵךְ֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְקָר֣וֹב לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ מִתֵּ֥ת הַכְּסִילִ֖ים זָ֑בַח כִּֽי־ אֵינָ֥ם יוֹדְעִ֖ים לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רָֽע׃

passages.text: Do not be quick to speak, and do not be hasty in your heart to utter a word before God. After all, God is in heaven and you are on earth. So let your words be few.
passages.sermon:
God is in heaven.
You are on earth.
Do not speak quickly.
Do not let your heart rush to say something before God.
Keep your words few.
passages.original: אַל־ תְּבַהֵ֨ל עַל־ פִּ֜יךָ וְלִבְּךָ֧ אַל־ יְמַהֵ֛ר לְהוֹצִ֥יא דָבָ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים בַּשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְאַתָּ֣ה עַל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ עַֽל־ כֵּ֛ן יִהְי֥וּ דְבָרֶ֖יךָ מְעַטִּֽים׃

passages.text: As a dream comes through many cares, so the speech of a fool comes with many words.
passages.sermon:
A dream comes when a person has many worries.
A fool speaks when he uses many words.
Many words show foolishness.
Many worries bring dreams.
passages.original: כִּ֛י בָּ֥א הַחֲל֖וֹם בְּרֹ֣ב עִנְיָ֑ן וְק֥וֹל כְּסִ֖יל בְּרֹ֥ב דְּבָרִֽים׃

passages.text: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.
passages.sermon:
God is holy and powerful.
God listens to your promises.
When you make a vow to God, act quickly.
Do not wait to fulfill your vow.
God does not delight in fools.
A fool does not keep promises.
If you make a vow, keep it.
Fulfill what you promise to God.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ תִּדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר לֵֽאלֹהִ֗ים אַל־ תְּאַחֵר֙ לְשַׁלְּמ֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין חֵ֖פֶץ בַּכְּסִילִ֑ים אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ תִּדֹּ֖ר שַׁלֵּֽם׃

passages.text: It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.
passages.sermon:
A vow is a promise made to God.
God expects people to keep their promises to Him.
It is better for a person not to make a vow to God.
It is worse to make a vow and not fulfill it.
Do not promise God something if you will not do it.
passages.original: ט֖וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ תִדֹּ֑ר מִשֶׁתִּדּ֖וֹר וְלֹ֥א תְשַׁלֵּֽם׃

passages.text: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?
passages.sermon:
God hears every word you speak.
God judges your actions.
Do not let your mouth lead you to sin.
Do not let your words cause your body to do wrong.
Do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake.
Do not make excuses for breaking your promise.
God can become angry with your words.
God can destroy the work you have done.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּתֵּ֤ן אֶת־ פִּ֙יךָ֙ לַחֲטִ֣יא אֶת־ בְּשָׂרֶ֔ךָ וְאַל־ תֹּאמַר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמַּלְאָ֔ךְ כִּ֥י שְׁגָגָ֖ה הִ֑יא לָ֣מָּה יִקְצֹ֤ף הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־ קוֹלֶ֔ךָ וְחִבֵּ֖ל אֶת־ מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: For as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. Therefore, fear God.
passages.sermon:
Many dreams do not have value.
Many words can also be empty.
Both dreams and many words can be useless.
You must fear God.
passages.original: כִּ֣י בְרֹ֤ב חֲלֹמוֹת֙ וַהֲבָלִ֔ים וּדְבָרִ֖ים הַרְבֵּ֑ה כִּ֥י אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְרָֽא׃

passages.text: If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.
passages.sermon:
If you see poor people being oppressed, do not be surprised.
If you see justice and righteousness being denied in your land, do not be surprised.
Many officials have power over others.
Each official is watched by someone higher.
There are always higher authorities above them.
passages.original: אִם־ עֹ֣שֶׁק רָ֠שׁ וְגֵ֨זֶל מִשְׁפָּ֤ט וָצֶ֙דֶק֙ תִּרְאֶ֣ה בַמְּדִינָ֔ה אַל־ תִּתְמַ֖הּ עַל־ הַחֵ֑פֶץ כִּ֣י גָבֹ֜הַּ מֵעַ֤ל גָּבֹ֙הַ֙ שֹׁמֵ֔ר וּגְבֹהִ֖ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: The produce of the earth is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.
passages.sermon: The earth produces food for everyone.\r\nAll people benefit from the land.\r\nEven the king depends on the fields for his gain.
passages.original: וְיִתְר֥וֹן אֶ֖רֶץ בַּכֹּ֣ל הִיא מֶ֥לֶךְ לְשָׂדֶ֖ה נֶעֱבָֽד׃

passages.text: He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.
passages.sermon: A person who loves money will never be satisfied with money.\r\nA person who loves wealth will never be satisfied with what he gains.\r\nThis is also meaningless.
passages.original: אֹהֵ֥ב כֶּ֙סֶף֙ לֹא־ יִשְׂבַּ֣ע כֶּ֔סֶף וּמִֽי־ אֹהֵ֥ב בֶּהָמ֖וֹן לֹ֣א תְבוּאָ֑ה גַּם־ זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: When good things increase, so do those who consume them; what then is the profit to the owner, except to behold them with his eyes?
passages.sermon: When good things increase, more people consume them.\r\nThe owner does not gain more from this increase.\r\nThe owner’s only benefit is to see the goods with his eyes.
passages.original: בִּרְבוֹת֙ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה רַבּ֖וּ אוֹכְלֶ֑יהָ וּמַה־ כִּשְׁרוֹן֙ לִבְעָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֖י אִם־ רְאִיַּת עֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: The sleep of the worker is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich man permits him no sleep.
passages.sermon:
A worker sleeps well.
His sleep is sweet.
He may eat little.
He may eat much.
He still sleeps well.
A rich man has much wealth.
His abundance keeps him awake.
He cannot sleep.
passages.original: מְתוּקָה֙ שְׁנַ֣ת הָעֹבֵ֔ד אִם־ מְעַ֥ט וְאִם־ הַרְבֵּ֖ה יֹאכֵ֑ל וְהַשָּׂבָע֙ לֶֽעָשִׁ֔יר אֵינֶ֛נּוּ מַנִּ֥יחַֽ ל֖וֹ לִישֽׁוֹן׃

passages.text: There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner, or wealth lost in a failed venture, so when that man has a son there is nothing to pass on.
passages.sermon:
I have seen a terrible evil under the sun.
A man keeps his wealth for himself.
This wealth harms him.
Sometimes, the man loses his wealth in a bad business deal.
Then the man has a son.
He has nothing left to give his son.
passages.original: יֵ֚שׁ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עֹ֛שֶׁר שָׁמ֥וּר לִבְעָלָ֖יו לְרָעָתֽוֹ׃ וְאָבַ֛ד הָעֹ֥שֶׁר הַה֖וּא בְּעִנְיַ֣ן רָ֑ע וְהוֹלִ֣יד בֵּ֔ן וְאֵ֥ין בְּיָד֖וֹ מְאֽוּמָה׃

passages.text: As a man came from his mother’s womb, so he will depart again, naked as he arrived. He takes nothing for his labor to carry in his hands.
passages.sermon:
A man is born from his mother’s womb.
He is naked when he is born.
He will leave this world in the same way.
He will be naked when he departs.
He cannot take anything with him from his work.
He will carry nothing in his hands when he goes.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יָצָא֙ מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמּ֔וֹ עָר֛וֹם יָשׁ֥וּב לָלֶ֖כֶת כְּשֶׁבָּ֑א וּמְא֙וּמָה֙ לֹא־ יִשָּׂ֣א בַעֲמָל֔וֹ שֶׁיֹּלֵ֖ךְ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: This too is a grievous evil: Exactly as a man is born, so he will depart. What does he gain as he toils for the wind?
passages.sermon:
A man is born into this world with nothing.
He will leave this world in the same way.
He takes nothing with him when he departs.
This is a great and painful evil.
A man works hard all his life.
He gains nothing lasting from his labor.
All his effort is like chasing the wind.
passages.original: וְגַם־ זֹה֙ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה כָּל־ עֻמַּ֥ת שֶׁבָּ֖א כֵּ֣ן יֵלֵ֑ךְ וּמַה־ יִּתְר֣וֹן ל֔וֹ שֶֽׁיַּעֲמֹ֖ל לָרֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and anger.
passages.sermon:
The man lives all his days in darkness.
He eats in darkness.
He has much sorrow.
He suffers sickness.
He feels anger.
passages.original: גַּ֥ם כָּל־ יָמָ֖יו בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יֹאכֵ֑ל וְכָעַ֥ס הַרְבֵּ֖ה וְחָלְי֥וֹ וָקָֽצֶף׃

passages.text: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him—for this is his lot.
passages.sermon:
God gives each person a limited number of days to live.
God gives each person life under the sun.
It is good to eat.
It is good to drink.
It is good to find satisfaction in your work.
A person should enjoy the results of his labor.
This is the portion God has given him.
This is fitting and right.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־ רָאִ֣יתִי אָ֗נִי ט֣וֹב אֲשֶׁר־ יָפֶ֣ה לֶֽאֶכוֹל־ וְ֠לִשְׁתּוֹת וְלִרְא֨וֹת טוֹבָ֜ה בְּכָל־ עֲמָל֣וֹ׀ שֶׁיַּעֲמֹ֣ל תַּֽחַת־ הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ מִסְפַּ֧ר יְמֵי־ חַיָּו אֲשֶׁר־ נָֽתַן־ ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־ ה֥וּא חֶלְקֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Furthermore, God has given riches and wealth to every man, and He has enabled him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor. This is a gift from God.
passages.sermon:
God gives some people riches and wealth.
God also gives them the power to enjoy these things.
God allows them to accept their share in life.
God lets them rejoice in their work.
This ability is a gift from God.
passages.original: גַּ֣ם כָּֽל־ הָאָדָ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן־ ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֩ עֹ֨שֶׁר וּנְכָסִ֜ים וְהִשְׁלִיט֨וֹ לֶאֱכֹ֤ל מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ וְלָשֵׂ֣את אֶת־ חֶלְק֔וֹ וְלִשְׂמֹ֖חַ בַּעֲמָל֑וֹ זֹ֕ה מַתַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃

passages.text: For a man seldom considers the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.
passages.sermon:
A man does not often think about the days of his life.
God fills his heart with joy.
God keeps him busy with this joy.
God causes him to focus on gladness instead of counting his days.
passages.original: כִּ֚י לֹ֣א הַרְבֵּ֔ה יִזְכֹּ֖ר אֶת־ יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֑יו כִּ֧י הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים מַעֲנֶ֖ה בְּשִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ׃
